messages:
laura.pm: Quick sync — we need a concrete acceptance checklist for the upcoming release (not 'GA' phrasing). Focus: SLA/SLO targets, docs handoff, oncall/escalation, monitoring alerts, and pricing gating. I sketched a minimal proposal below.

mike-eng: Thanks — can you paste the sketch here?

laura.pm: Sure. High level items: 1) SLOs defined per route (p95 latency, error rate), 2) SLA commit levels for paid tiers, 3) runbook & oncall owner, 4) alerting thresholds + dashboards, 5) docs & SDK samples, 6) pricing table and migration guidance, 7) rollout plan and rollback criteria.

deepa-ml: For models routing: we should call out degraded-mode behavior explicitly — e.g., fallback to smaller model with note on cost/quality tradeoffs. That impacts SLOs (soft vs hard).

sanjay-sre: Agree on fallback. Also propose these SLOs as a starting point: `p95 latency < 300ms` for "interactive" routes, `error rate < 0.5%` (5xx + timeout), and `queue wait < 50ms` for dedicated pools. We should mark which are "operational" vs "commercial" commitments.

mike-eng: Those numbers seem optimistic for some workloads. Can we admit a tiered SLA: bronze/silver/gold with differing latency windows and support response times?

laura.pm: Yes — tiered SLA. Draft commercial commitments: gold = 99.95% uptime & 100ms faster p95 target for select routes, silver = 99.9% & baseline p95, bronze = 99.5% best-effort. Need legal + finance alignment but want engineering agreement on measurability.

emily-docs: For docs handoff: I need clear owner for each doc artifact. Suggest: API reference (mike-eng), quickstart + migration guide (product + devex), runbooks (sre + eng). ETA request: drafts by EOW next Tue?

sanjay-sre: Runbooks: include these sections — symptoms, mitigation steps (hotfix + rollback), postmortem checklist, escalation matrix (pager -> oncall lead -> eng manager -> exec). Also include playbook snippet for model fallback.

laura.pm: Good. For monitoring/alerts let's list required dashboards: per-route latency histogram, p95/p99 trends, error-rate heatmap, capacity utilization, prefix-cache hit rate, model-fallback count. Alert rules: page at sustained breach > 5m or burst > 3x baseline.

deepa-ml: Add quality/regression alert: monitor eval prompt sets for drift (token-level logloss or delta in passrate). If drop > 2% over 1h roll back or trigger investigation.

mike-eng: On pricing gating: we should lock the published pricing rows (per-token + embeddings) and a migration path when we change quantization or batching defaults. Finance wants a conservative committed discount plan for Dedicated customers.

laura.pm: Action items and owners I propose: 1) Finalize SLO table (mike-eng, sanjay-sre) - due Fri, 2) Draft SLA legal wording (laura.pm + legal) - due Mon, 3) Runbooks (sanjay-sre + mike-eng) - due Tue, 4) Docs draft (emily-docs) - due Tue, 5) Monitoring dashboards (sanjay-sre) - due Fri, 6) Pricing rows + migration notes (mike-eng + finance) - due Wed.

emily-docs: I'll start doc skeleton now. pls drop w/owners into the doc when ready.

ops-bot: Reminder: create #incident-playbooks channel and add runbook links when ready.

laura.pm: One open question — do we require a formal customer beta (2–4 customers) before committing commercial SLA? Opinions?

mike-eng: Strong yes. We need real world traffic to validate routing/fallback. Recommend closed beta with 3 customers representing interactive, batch, and high-throughput embedding workloads.

sanjay-sre: Beta should run for 3 weeks with predefined test harness + SLO smoke tests. If we pass, we gradate to commercial.

deepa-ml: I'll own the test harness prompts and evaluation thresholds.

laura.pm: OK. I'll collate and publish a single acceptance checklist doc and ping reviewers. Thanks everyone — I'll update the doc with owners/timestamps and a short 'go/no-go' rubric for product review on next Wed. :white_check_mark:
